painful ecchymotic lesion on his left calf

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of arthralgias, skin lesions, and positive autoantibodies, along with the presence of antiphospholipid antibodies, are consistent with antiphospholipid syndrome.
The patient's symptoms of fever, chills, and worsening dyspnea, along with the positive FilmArray respiratory panel for RSV, are consistent with RSV infection.
The patient's symptoms of hemoptysis, ecchymoses, and vasculopathy on biopsy are consistent with vasculitis.
The patient's symptoms of arthralgias, weight loss, and positive autoantibodies, along with the presence of antinuclear antibodies, are consistent with systemic lupus erythematosus.

rationales.F03: Hemoptysis is more common in vasculitis.
rationales.F05: Intermittent night sweats can be seen in systemic lupus erythematosus.
rationales.F06: Arthralgias can be seen in systemic lupus erythematosus.
rationales.F07: Weight loss can be seen in systemic lupus erythematosus.
rationales.F08: Painful ecchymotic lesions can be seen in antiphospholipid syndrome and vasculitis.
rationales.F12: Multifocal alveolar infiltrates can be seen in respiratory syncytial virus infection.

frontier_selector.rationale: Positive lupus anticoagulant, elevated anticardiolipin IgM, and anti–phosphatidylserine IgM, along with clinical findings of thrombotic paucicellular vasculopathy and ecchymoses, support the diagnosis of Antiphospholipid syndrome.
